newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - API to show building distillate supplies.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - API to show building distillate supplies.

text.p: Tuesday evening's data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected to show a bearish build in distillate stocks, confirming the view of replenishing inventories which has been behind the decline in heating oil prices since last two weeks.
"We are narrowing the supply gap, especially the shortfall in PADD1 (the northeast U.S.)," said Fimat USA Futures analyst Rita Beale.
A Reuters survey shows an overall distillate stock build of between one and three million barrels for the week ended Oct 25.

Meanwhile, gasoline stocks are seen down by between one and three million barrels at a record-low. Crude is expected to build between one and two million barrels, a reflection of lower refinery runs which are seen about one percentage point lower.
The drop in gasoline stocks is not expected to trigger a big price rise in that sector is "out-of-season" and in any case the market has been coping with near record-low stocks for some time.

"Distillates will be the focus regardless of the gasoline inventories. The gasoline situation is just short term since we have been near this low before and been ok," said John Bradberry, vice president at oil distributor Continental Ozark Inc.
Last week, total distillate stocks, comprised mainly of heating oil and deisel, were 16.3 million barrels below year-ago levels.

Though the data showed a decline in total distillate stocks, heating oil stocks increased due to record distillate output of 3.7 million barrels a day, particularly in the key U.S. northeast market. However, stocks still were some 15 million barrels below a year ago and some market participants see the market continuing to focus on the shortfall in the northeast.
"We are still in a very bullish mode going into the winter," said Fimat's Beale of heating oil's longer term fundamentals.
Political pressure and attractive margins have caused refineries to step up heating oil production at the expense of gasoline output.

"It's no secret that there was a major price incentive to make distillate," said a trader in Texas, adding that a glut of distillate barrels waiting to be shipped has since softened spot prices in the U.S. Gulf.
Refinery shutdowns due to seasonal maintanence and plant problems also cut gasoline production while allowing crude stocks to build and overall refinery capacity to drop.

Some traders and analysts cautioned that gasoline stocks could show a build in a corrective bounce to the six million barrel drop seen in last week's API data. But most argued the factors driving a draw in gasoline are too compelling for there to be a build.
